plan-protected-rejection-in-the-lean-mod.text: Plan: protected rejection in the Lean model, in four slices.

Ticket 494 under epic 498. Base e7b55ac9 (the plan was first written on e3c9ab01 and rebased on 13 October 2026), branch feat/494-protected-rejection-rule, worktree /code/singular-issue-494. Read the specification for what must hold, the rulings for why, the research for the evidence behind the tables below, and the touch list for the files. No coder starts before the rebased plan has been reviewed.

status.text: Planning artifacts written, committed locally and rebased onto the current main. The one open question is settled: the public suite shows the in-window rejection of a foldable request as unmet by ruling until the validators change (decision B, recorded in the mandate and the decisions). The gate had two independent authors, synthesized once in the gate; the rebase moved line numbers and added hosted jobs, and the gate page records which rows that touched.

story.text: As the person accepting this ticket, I read one page and learn what changes in which order, what the eight red checks of the earlier attempt mean, what happens to that attempt, and where the work can collide with other lanes, so that I can approve the plan without reading the model.

strategy.text: The earlier attempt put the whole rule, its batch semantics and every consumer into one change on a tree that has since lost five of its seven edges. This plan ports the same reviewed design onto the two-edge model in four vertical slices. Each slice leaves the repository green by regenerating the copies its own change moves, and each ends in something a person can run: the model runner, a conformance row, or the public page.
Slices three and four are independent after slice two. The rule is pushed for hosted checks after slice one, after slice three (which completes the rejection rule) and after slice four.

the-four-slices.text: Each slice is sized for one commit owner run, with the inner loop on lake build of the changed modules and the gate's own commands run once per candidate. A slice that runs for hours without a product commit is cut again, not supervised harder.
Slice one is the smallest. Slice two carries the weight of the proofs and is where the historical scenario is run before and after.

the-eight-red-checks-of-the-earlier-atte.text: The eight red checks of the earlier attempt.

Each check failed at a7224021 on an assertion found in the hosted log (see the research page for the line). Each was green at the attempt's own base 23964e66 and on main at e3c9ab01, so the attempt introduced it and none is flaky. The classes are named for what they mean, with the epic owner's letter in parentheses: moves-with-the-model (a), where the model change contradicts an expectation that must move with it in this ticket; needs-the-validators (b), where the expectation can only hold once ticket 495 changes the validators; stale-against-main (c), fixed by re-deriving on the current main; and other (d). The table says which slice cures each.

Re-checked on 13 October 2026 against main at e7b55ac9: all eight hosted jobs still exist under the same names and run the same commands, and none of the merged lanes removed a cause (the model files and the rows' scripts are byte-identical to e3c9ab01 apart from the proof idiom of the toolchain bump), so the classification stands.

Only the in-window rejection of a foldable request cannot be made to agree by this ticket. Decision B publishes it as unmet, in the generic session's standing unmet row; the eight checks themselves end green, and a tripwire turns red the day the chain starts to refuse it.

what-happens-to-pull-request-508.text: Settled at the coding release of 13 October 2026: this branch re-derives the change and supersedes 508. This branch's pull request names the superseded head a7224021 in its body, and 508 is closed once that pull request exists; the ticket owner does not close it. The reasons: its base was 74 commits and 514 files behind the plan's first base and models seven edges; a rebase would conflict in every Lean file and every generated corpus, and the corpus is regenerated anyway; its constitution amendment collides in number and content with the one on main; and its design is not lost, because this plan ports it name for name (the data model lists the one difference) and its two source reviews stay in the epic's record as evidence for the design, not for the new code. The branch feat/protected-rejection is kept, never deleted, as historical evidence.

ordering-and-the-other-lanes.text: This ticket sits in the validators-and-Lean surface of the merge queue: after 505 (merged), before 495, 529 and 506, which stay strictly serial behind it. The command-line split (528) has merged. It rebases only at a safe boundary after each merge and never under a running coder. The touch list names the shared surfaces, which lane owns each, and the files that live lanes also change.

a-neighbouring-defect-the-approval-a-rej.text: A neighbouring defect: the approval a reject returns.

Ticket 532 reports that a reject sends the request's approval to the folder's change, not the owner's refund. The base model states otherwise: a rejection's owner output commits to the request's approval asset name, and the rule of this ticket keeps that exactly, because an admitted rejection is proved equal to the base exit. The comparison row that would expose the builder is placed with ticket 496, not here. Reason: the defect is in the builder, so such a row fails on every reject the suite builds until 496 lands, which would put one builder defect on every reject row of slices two and three and tie this ticket's gate to a repair it cannot make; the row and its fix belong in one change so the row's tripwire is the fix. If the epic owner wants the row here, it is a fifth slice that makes the reject comparison read the approval and records each reject row as a divergence until 496.

decision-b-and-what-it-changes.text: Decision B and what it changes.

The question was what the suite shows for the in-window row until the validators change. The answer is option B. The dedicated row becomes a lawful rejection at once, with lifecycle evidence, of a request that cannot be folded, which model and chain both accept. The generic session's standing unmet row books a foldable insertion, the model refuses its rejection inside the windows while the chain accepts it, and the row stays published as unmet with a tripwire that ticket 495 must flip. This ticket merges alone, ahead of ticket 495. Options A (hold the push until 495) and C are not taken. Slice three's direction and the last gate rows follow from this decision.

after-slice-three-the-economic-model-and.text: After slice three: the economic model and the paper.

Operator order of 13 October 2026: the model states the whole economic design and a formal paper explains it, and slices five to eight run before slice four. The design records the amounts and the attacks; the economics plan lists the theorems, the ones expected to fail, six more slices and the paper. The desk reviews that plan before any of it is built.

budget-and-ceilings.text: One team per epic at a time: the coder is Muse and the persistent auditor Grok, both launched only after the rebased plan is reviewed. The operator is on credits; no seat beyond those named is authorized, and while the GLM quota is out (until 14 October 2026) no seat alternates or races.
